prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Caldera Wildfire Detection and Suppression Support System (WUI, steep terrain). Baseline: segmentation, time sync, health checks; coordination records keep timestamps, participants, radio path; favor command continuity over automation when impaired. Security: Portal named accounts, role-based auth, MFA when auth reachable, else signed auto-expiring emergency credentials reviewed after restoration; least privilege for actors; production config admin separately approved, never field accounts. Append-only audit store (logons, role changes, queued releases, model changes, overrides: time/user/device/network/record/outcome); field components buffer signed audit records, forward unmodified. Maintenance record precedes equipment status change. Retention: operational records per agency incident period; raw sensor data shorter; encryption at rest, controlled export, authorized deletion. Multi-period incidents: staged spares/power/network/cleaning supplies/recovery procedures; no single fault stops operations. Actors: Duty Detection Officer, Air Attack Supervisor, Tanker Base Manager, Helitack Crew Leader (Crewline Mobile Tablet: acknowledgments, location; uses Crew Staging Pin in drills), Drone Pilot Operator, County Emergency Liaison. Role-based training before each season and on procedure/config change. Elements: Caldera Incident Command Portal (Emberhall): common picture, Crew Staging Pin, triage, marks failed radio route impaired (Orion acknowledges), assignment packages, flags assignments on Confirmed Ignition perimeter/priority change; Disconnected Operating Mode (last sync, queued updates, no irreversible releases). North/South Lookout Camera Masts: heartbeat, temperature, storage, pointing telemetry; North: Thermal Spot Snippet; South: Camera Cleaning Log to Smoke Classifier Module (advisory if mast unavailable/low quality; human confirmation required). Horizon Ridge Drone Dock (Kestrel): Battery Swap Ticket to Drone Pilot Operator. Drone Tasking Service: pending/active/complete; no flight release; avoids Marigold lanes; corridor permit check in degraded comms. Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine (Lantern): detections, recommendations, Ridge Shadow Mask, may down-weight Smoke Classifier, keeps last approved model, rejects unsigned/unversioned. MesoWest Weather Fusion Node (Brindle): Wind Shift Bulletin to Redtail, exposure flags, cache. VHF Radio Gateway Repeater (Badger): fallback aviation relay, mirrors assignment summaries, queues acknowledgments ≥15 min. Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console (Marigold): blocks incomplete releases; Runway Release Note; Suppression Drop Receipt. East

New part:
S211: All operational users shall receive communications training that includes VHF Radio Gateway Repeater failure modes, alternate contact paths, call signs, message brevity, and confirmation readbacks.
S212: Weather training shall explain how the MesoWest Weather Fusion Node supports situational awareness and how operators should treat weather inputs when local observations conflict with displayed values.
S213: Initial qualification shall include supervised console practice, scenario walkthroughs, and a documented check by an instructor who is authorized by the operations lead.
S214: Annual refresher training shall include changes to software screens, revised thresholds, updated contact rosters, seasonal hazard briefings, and lessons learned from prior incidents.
S215: Tabletop exercises shall be conducted before the expected peak fire period and shall test detection triage, command notification, airspace coordination, tanker-base coordination, crew deployment, and public-agency liaison actions.
S216: Live exercises shall be scheduled at least once per season when conditions permit and shall include field crews, aircraft coordination staff, drone operations staff, and command-center personnel.
S217: Exercise controllers shall inject realistic complications such as intermittent network service, obscured camera views, delayed field confirmation, resource conflicts, and conflicting reports from external observers.
S218: Performance measures shall include time from automated detection to human review, time from review to command notification, time to resource assignment, communication completion rate, and accuracy of incident status updates.
S219: Detection quality shall be evaluated using confirmed events, benign smoke sources, weather-related artifacts, and operator notes so that both missed detections and false alarms are visible to program management.
S220: Every false-alarm review shall identify the apparent cause, affected sensors or analytic outputs, operator actions, dispatch consequences, and any recommended tuning or training change.
S221: The review board shall include operations, aviation, field crew, maintenance, and county liaison representatives when the event affected more than one operational function.
S222: Seasonal readiness shall require each active user to demonstrate current proficiency, complete required safety briefings, and acknowledge the current operating procedures before receiving operational access.
S223: Personnel who do not meet proficiency requirements shall complete remedial training and a repeat evaluation before performing unsupervised duties in the Caldera Wildfire Detection and Suppression Support System.
S224: Deployment governance for the Caldera Wildfire Detection and Suppression Support System shall be managed as a staged release process that follows completion of seasonal readiness activities.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
